title: Associated germs detect sections on opens of Noetherian affine schemes
statement: Let R be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], V an open of Spec R [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and s a structure-sheaf section on V. If the germ of s at every q in V whose prime ideal is associated to R is zero, then s=0.

source.place: Tags 0311 and 0310 (associated-prime localization), principal affine cover and affine stalk localization

proof.text: First prove the affine-global case. Transport the section through ΓSpecIso to r in R. The stalk at each associated prime is its prime localization; vanishing yields a denominator outside the prime annihilating r. The injective product-of-localizations criterion makes r zero. For arbitrary V, at each x choose D(g) contained in V. Identify D(g) with Spec R_g. Associated primes of R_g contract to associated primes of R by Noetherian associated-prime localization. Pull the section to Spec R_g; germ_stalkMap transfers the hypothesis, and the affine-global case kills this pullback. The map Spec R_g to V is an open immersion, so its stalk map is an isomorphism and the germ at x is zero. Sheaf section_ext finishes. Includes empty V and the zero ring.

lean.statement:
theorem eq_zero_of_associated_germs
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (V : (Spec (.of R)).Opens) (s : Γ(V.toScheme, ⊤))
    (hs : ∀ (q : Spec (.of R)) (hq : q ∈ V),
      q.asIdeal ∈ associatedPrimes R R →
        (V.toScheme.presheaf.Γgerm ⟨q, hq⟩).hom s = 0) :
    s = 0
